analysis.title: Equities - Tactical Top Picks (Unified Global Markets PMA Equity Sales, 16 Nov 2026)
key_insights: UBS lists 10 open Tactical Top Picks as of 16 Nov 2026. They are Accelleron (CHF 93.5 PT), Prysmian (EUR 175), Rolls-Royce (GBP 19), Barclays (GBP 5.7), NVIDIA (USD 300), Netflix (USD 100), Edwards Lifesciences (USD 118), Oracle (USD 250), Boeing (USD 240) and Mitsubishi Heavy Industries (JPY 5,240). All carry a Buy rating, and all except Edwards and Netflix are also flagged CIO Most Preferred (MP).
Four ideas are marked NEW on 16-17 Nov 2026: Accelleron, Prysmian, NVIDIA and Mitsubishi Heavy Industries. Their return since inception is not yet available.

Return since inception to 13 Nov 2026 for the open ideas that have a price: Oracle +5.1%, Edwards +2.3%, Rolls-Royce +1.4%, Netflix -2.8%, Barclays -9.9%, Boeing -11.0%. Barclays (inception 14 Sep) and Boeing (inception 5 Oct) are the two laggards. Each sits below its indicative lower exit level (Barclays GBP 4.08, Boeing USD 163.81 against current prices of 4.3135 and 171.5, so still inside the band, with Boeing close to it).

NVIDIA: UBS says Nvidia could deliver above-consensus Q3 earnings on 17 Nov 2026, supported by supply-constrained AI demand. September Taiwan exports surged above seasonality. UBS sees significant upside to demand if supply and powered data center capacity become available, and says semiconductor valuations have derated sharply despite accelerating AI demand. A CEO change is not expected to alter the long-term product roadmap.

Accelleron: UBS highlights data center gas-engine demand as a key medium-term tailwind (Accelleron holds more than 80% share), strong marine demand from Chinese new-build activity, and marine capex growth of about 15% in 2027. Service is about 75% of group revenue. Equipment growth pressures near-term mix, and installed units should lift service margins around 2030.

Prysmian: UBS expects 2027 earnings upgrades. About 25% of fibre contracts still await pricing updates, and Transmission margins are expected to rise toward 24-25% by 2030 from 20-21%. Prysmian is the US leader in low-voltage data centre cable. Catalysts are 2 more hyperscaler fibre agreements and a Q2 2027 capital markets day. Valuation has reset toward its long-run average after the recent derating.

Rolls-Royce: UBS calls the turnaround incomplete and expects further earnings upgrades. FY26 results around 23 Feb 2027 may bring higher medium-term cash flow guidance. UBS expects Civil Aerospace margins to reach levels comparable with top peers and Defence profitability to exceed most peers, with Power Systems helped by data centre backup demand.

Barclays: UBS sees investment banking momentum, structural hedging earnings resilience, cost actions and attractive distributions. It says Barclays looks undervalued versus peers. The target uses a sum-of-the-parts approach on 2027 divisional profit estimates.

Edwards Lifesciences: UBS cites strong Q3 results, durable transcatheter aortic valve replacement growth (74% of sales), the PROGRESS trial, and mitral and tricuspid therapies as a growth engine. An Investor Day on 4 Dec 2026 is the next catalyst. The USD 118 target assumes about 32x Q5-Q8 EPS.

Netflix: UBS says Q3 revenues were in line and profits ahead. It argues estimates are moderating while the long-term case is intact. Cited drivers are US content execution, advertising monetization, live events, licensing, margin expansion and free cash flow. Netflix is down 2.8% since inception on 9 Nov 2026.

Boeing: UBS cites a backlog of nearly USD 750bn, conservative guidance that leaves scope to outperform through 2029, and free cash flow rising from USD 2.2bn in 2026 to USD 15.1bn by 2030. The stock is down 11.0% since the 5 Oct inception. Stated risks include weaker air travel, share loss to Airbus or COMAC, supply chain problems, and defense deterioration. The target reflects 20.5x EV/EBITDA.

Oracle: the one-pager's investment-case bullets repeat the Boeing text (the backlog and USD 2.2bn to USD 15.1bn free cash flow bullets), so they cannot be attributed to Oracle. The company profile and valuation statement are Oracle's. The price target uses a free cash flow multiple. UBS names upside risks from share gains against Workday and SAP, and downside risks from a recent sales reorganization, possibly slipped deals, limited traction in Oracle's cloud offering and tougher competition. Oracle is up 5.1% since inception on 2 Nov 2026.

Mitsubishi Heavy Industries: UBS raised its price target to JPY 5,240 and reiterated Buy on 12 Nov 2026. It says Energy Systems earnings are entering an expansion phase led by gas turbine profits, with order prices up 20% y/y in H1. A JPY 300bn buyback covers 3.6% of shares. The target is based on a FY3/28E PER of 30x.

Track record (UBS-reported): 278 closed ideas since inception with average absolute performance of 1.2% and relative performance of 0.2%, and an average of 39 trading days per idea. 2026 YTD closed ideas average -0.5% absolute and -1.7% relative in Europe, -1.0% and -2.1% in the Americas, -6.2% and -4.1% in Asia-Pacific, and +7.2% and +3.7% in Switzerland.

Document is a sales-desk marketing product, not independent research. The disclosures say it is prepared by sales or trading personnel, is not a product of the Research Department, and may differ from IB Research or GWM views. Each idea has indicative exit bands tied to beta: for example +12%/-9% for Accelleron and +20%/-15% for Prysmian, NVIDIA and Mitsubishi Heavy.

sector_views.sector: AI data center power and infrastructure
sector_views.rationale: Four of the ten picks (Accelleron, Prysmian, Rolls-Royce Power Systems and Mitsubishi Heavy gas turbines) are tied to data center power demand, in addition to NVIDIA and Oracle on the compute and cloud side.
UBS says semiconductor valuations have derated sharply despite accelerating AI demand.
Barclays is a Top Pick, and the Barclays valuation statement cites an overweight stance on EU banks.

earnings_insights: NVIDIA: Q3 earnings due 17 Nov 2026. UBS says the company could deliver above-consensus results (UBS expectation, not a print).
Netflix: UBS says Q3 revenues were in line and profits ahead (reported Q3 result, per UBS). It says estimates moderate while long-term upside remains intact.
Edwards Lifesciences: UBS cites strong Q3 results across key franchises and profitability (reported Q3). Investor Day is on 4 Dec 2026.
Rolls-Royce: FY26 results are expected around 23 Feb 2027. UBS sees potential for higher medium-term cash flow guidance and a guidance upgrade (forecast).
Prysmian: the 3Q conference call (UBS note dated 29 Oct 2026) offered line of sight on 2027 upgrades. A Q2 2027 capital markets day is a further catalyst.
Mitsubishi Heavy Industries: UBS's target uses a FY3/28E PER of 30x. Gas turbine order prices rose 20% y/y in H1.

Boeing: UBS forecasts free cash flow of USD 2.2bn in 2026 rising to USD 15.1bn by 2030 (estimate). The valuation statement notes a 0% YTD adjusted EBIT margin after charges on major development programs.

risk_factors: Accelleron: cyclical downturn in global marine investment and shipping fleet utilization, FX translation, regional regulation and raw material prices.
Prysmian: grid margins falling from elevated levels, slower high voltage Transmission growth to 2028, and US price competition at Encore Wire.
Rolls-Royce: forecasts depend on air traffic, national defence expenditure and exchange rates.
Barclays: high exposure to UK macroeconomic conditions, credit and interest rate risk, capital markets volatility and regulatory change.
NVIDIA: competition from AMD and Intel, and cyclicality of semiconductor revenue and corporate profitability.
Edwards: competitive device launches, pricing pressure, clinical trial delays, hospital capacity constraints and pharmacologic therapies.
Netflix: US economy and consumer expectations, international exposure and FX translation.
Oracle: sales reorganization execution risk, slipped deals, limited cloud traction and tougher competition.
Boeing: weaker air travel, share loss to Airbus and COMAC, supply chain issues causing delivery halts, and defense business deterioration.
Mitsubishi Heavy: sluggish capex across Japan, Europe, the US and China, higher labour, logistics and material costs, and a worse competitive environment.
Document-level: past performance is not a reliable indicator, and fees and currency fluctuations are not considered in the reported returns.
